0.content: Tighnari is Cyno's best friend, as Kaveh discovered when Tighnari's "best friend" turned out to be an intimidating Matra. Cyno respects him as a scholar with total dedication to knowledge who never crosses important boundaries and respects every form of life. Cyno supported his choice to decline an Akademiya post. Tighnari can hear him sneaking into Gandharva Ville to check on Collei. He warns people that being chased by Cyno is the nightmare of a lifetime, and he once banned jokes at dinner; Cyno told three in a row and his food went cold.

1.content: In the official manga, Lisa wrote to her old teacher Cyrus about a Fatui document concerning the god remains injected into Collei. The Akademiya sent Cyno, who reached Mondstadt three days later and sealed the remains at Starsnatch Cliff in an agonising ritual. He then took Collei back to Sumeru and left her in Tighnari's care. Cyno calls her endurance admirable. Collei is grateful but says the back of her neck starts hurting whenever she remembers the sealing. He keeps visiting to make sure she is doing well.

2.content: Cyrus is a retired Spantamad sage, a teacher to both Lisa and Cyno. He nearly died exploring the desert and was rescued by the Temple of Silence, but opposed Bamoun's plan to implant Hermanubis's fragments in children. He took the child Cyno away, adopted him, educated him and taught him to fit into society instead of treating him as a test subject. Cyno says he is very grateful. Cyrus also taught him that without law, wisdom becomes calamity. Lisa says Cyno inherited the professor's wit and eccentricities, and that Cyno in turn softened his stubborn ways.

3.comment: Cyno: Hermanubis and the Ba Fragments
3.content: Hermanubis was one of King Deshret's Seven Pillars, honoured as the Greatest of Sages and the guide of priests. After Deshret's fall he founded the Temple of Silence. When the Temple was besieged, he shattered himself to empower his followers. A fragment of his power dwells in Cyno, who calls it a spirit that he can let indwell his body as a vessel. Cyno says this is possible partly through his constitution and partly through a deal he willingly made, and that as a judge of souls he must put his own on the scales too.

4.comment: Cyno: The Matra and the Six Sins
4.content: The Matra are the Akademiya's disciplinary officers. They arrest researchers for plagiarism, bribery, fraud, misuse of funds and forbidden studies, and they inspect and seal goods such as Knowledge Capsules. Researchers call them "Paper Shredders" and "Mr. You-Can't-Do-This". Cyno liked "the Akademiya's Sumpter Beasts", saying they carry the rules on their backs and must always feel that weight. The laws rest on the six cardinal sins the early sages laid down after researchers began reshaping terrain, controlling weather and tampering with life and death.

5.comment: Cyno: The Fall of the Sages (3.1-3.2)
5.content: When Cyno found that Grand Sage Azar had submitted falsified data and was refused permission to investigate, he exiled himself and stepped down from his post to pursue it. In the desert he ambushed the Traveler and Alhaitham, suspecting them of the sages' business, until Dehya and Candace forced a truce at Aaru Village. Together they traced vanished "Village Keepers" (exiled mad scholars) to Eremites working for the sages. They learned that the sages and Dottore were building a new god.

6.content: Cyno's great passion. He started playing to stay balanced, explaining that a Matra's heart is like a bowstring that must be neither too slack nor too taut. He now considers the game an art form, creativity within a fixed rule set, and a rare way to read people honestly. He builds decks for friends, travelled to Fontaine for a TCG gathering's exclusive cardholders, and once agonised over whether a novel's hero who drew a non-existent card had broken the rules. He never goes easy on anyone, but he walks beginners through the game afterwards.
